:::{#def-turing-machine}
#### Turing machine

A **Turing machine** with $k \ge 2$ tapes consists of:

- $k$ tapes, each a sequence of cells that starts at a leftmost cell and goes on forever to the right,
  with one head per tape that reads and writes one cell at a time.
  The first tape is the *input tape*, which the machine can read but not write;
  the last tape is the *output tape*;
  any others are *work tapes*.
- A finite *alphabet* $A$ of the symbols a cell can hold.
  It includes the binary digits $0$ and $1$,
  a blank symbol $\square$,
  and a start symbol $\triangleright$.
- A finite set $Q$ of *states*,
  which includes a start state $q_{\text{start}}$
  and a halting state $q_{\text{halt}}$.
- A *transition function*,
  a map from $Q \times A^k$ to $Q \times A^{k - 1} \times \set{\text{L}, \text{S}, \text{R}}^k$.

The machine starts in state $q_{\text{start}}$ with every head on its tape's leftmost cell.
Each tape holds $\triangleright$ in its leftmost cell and blanks after it,
except that the input tape holds the input $x \in \set{0, 1}^*$ right after the $\triangleright$.
In one *step*, the machine reads its state and the $k$ symbols under its heads,
and the transition function gives a new state,
a symbol to write on each tape but the input tape,
and a move for each head:
one cell left (L), stay (S), or one cell right (R).
A head told to move left from the leftmost cell stays where it is.
The machine *halts* when it enters $q_{\text{halt}}$,
and its *output* is then the string of binary digits on the output tape,
read from the cell after $\triangleright$ up to the first symbol that is not $0$ or $1$
[@arora2009computational, section 1.2].

:::
